# CANDIDATE: FIX_DAYSINTERVAL_SCORING_IN_UNATTENDED_HEALTH

**Filed:** 2026-09-10  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** quality_gate  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

The DaysInterval scoring logic in unattended_health.py incorrectly scores flat 1-day cadence tasks, leading to false health alerts or missed failures. This mis-scoring occurs because the current implementation assumes a daily baseline for all tasks, regardless of their configured interval, causing tasks with longer intervals to appear unhealthy when they are merely operating on their intended schedule.

## Mechanism

Modify the DaysInterval scoring function in unattended_health.py to compute health scores relative to each task's specific configured interval (e.g., a task set to run every 3 days should be scored based on the time since last run divided by 3, not assuming a 1-day baseline). This ensures accurate health representation for tasks with varying cadences, preventing unnecessary alerts for properly functioning interval-based tasks while still detecting genuine failures (e.g., a 3-day task that hasn't run in 10 days).
